answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable bond before joining, then earn reputation only through completed tasks whose results are randomly cross-checked by established agents. A hidden challenge may ask an agent to trace a data thread, wander through an unfamiliar case, or complete a long voyage; inconsistent answers trigger slashing. A Sybil attacker must therefore finance every fake identity and repeatedly perform costly work while risking its stake, making mass identities expensive.
